prompt: Some players kill a boss 80 times without getting the item, while others get it on the first try. The unlucky ones quit.
tells: kill a boss 80 times without getting the item
why: Bad-luck protection raises the chance after each failure.
trap: The drop rate may be fine on average; the streaks are the problem.

prompt: A 20% critical hit chance sometimes produces five crits in a row, which feels broken.
why: Pseudo-random distribution spreads results more evenly.
trap: The average is right; the clumping is the issue.

prompt: Instead of random pieces, a puzzle game deals each of the 7 pieces once per bag, in random order.
tells: deals each of the 7 pieces once per bag
why: A shuffled bag controls randomness: varied but never starved.
trap: It's still random order, just within limits.

prompt: A gacha game guarantees a rare character after 90 pulls.
tells: guarantees a rare character after 90 pulls
why: A pity timer is bad-luck protection.
trap: It caps bad luck rather than changing the base rate.

prompt: An RPG gives random items, but players keep getting gear for classes they don't play.
tells: gear for classes they don't play
why: Weighting drops toward useful items controls randomness.
trap: Fixing stats wouldn't fix who the items are for.

prompt: Speedrunners want the same random level layout as their rivals, so the game offers a shared seed.
why: Seeds make randomness repeatable when fairness matters.
trap: Challenge is the fun; seeding is the randomness control.
